title: Seventh Integrated Household Living Conditions Survey (EICV7): Main Indicators Report 2023/24
publisher: National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda (NISR)
distributor: National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda (NISR), statistics.gov.rw
citation: National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda (NISR) (2025) Seventh Integrated Household Living Conditions Survey (EICV7) Report: NISR
fieldwork_period: October 2023 - October 2024 (12 months in nine cycles; pp. 11, 12, 15)
population: Household-based population of Rwanda; two-stage sample of 1,674 enumeration areas stratified by district, nine households per area (pp. 12, 15). Each estimate states its own denominator.
notes: sampleSize counts households: 15,054 households (62,110 people) were surveyed (p. 78). The data file is NISR's annex workbook; definitions and page references come from the report PDF (https://statistics.gov.rw/sites/default/files/documents/2025-07/EICV7_Main%20Indicator%20Report.pdf, SHA-256 6105321b6edaeac40df291d9b2450cec121cd0a0b7b750554aefabbfd5b2873c). The report gives only the year 2025; the workbook is dated 28 April 2025 and the PDF 9-10 July 2025. Poverty line: RWF 560,127 per adult equivalent per year in January 2024 prices (extreme poverty: RWF 356,432, the food poverty line) (pp. 17, 18, 79). EICV7 revised how consumption and poverty are measured (fewer visits, a 7-day food recall, food away from home, January 2024 household-level Paasche deflators, a new adult-equivalence scale and a poverty line built on 2,400 kcal/adult equivalent/day valued at second-quintile consumption patterns; p. 13), so EICV7 poverty rates are not directly comparable with earlier EICV publications (pp. 11, 13, 18). The report's comparison uses a modelled 2016/17 rate of 39.8% under the EICV7 method (Table 9.3, p. 82; 95% CI 37.7-41.4, model-dependent) against 27.4% in 2023/24, a fall of 12.4 percentage points; the originally published EICV5 rate was 38.2% (Table 0.1 note, p. 19). Those trend figures are not served as records here. Estimates are descriptive survey estimates with sampling error; differences between districts whose confidence intervals overlap may not be meaningful.
